title: Wrist warmers in the round
subtitle: Seamless 1x1 rib wrist warmers with a gusseted thumb hole.
excerpt: Wrist warmers in 1x1 rib worked in the round, with a small gusseted thumb opening. DK weight. Three sizes for wrist circumferences of 16, 18, and 20 cm.
sourceNotes: In-the-round wrist warmers with a thumb gusset are documented in Weldon's Practical Knitter from the 1880s. The specific construction here is a standard seamless pattern derived from public-domain sources.

knitting.gaugeText: 22 sts x 30 rounds = 10 x 10 cm in 1x1 rib slightly stretched on 3.75 mm needles.
knitting.finishedSizeText: Wrist circumference 16 (18, 20) cm. Length 18 cm on all sizes.

glossaryTerms.definition: A thumb opening made by increasing a wedge of stitches over several rounds at the thumb position, placing them on waste yarn, then working them as the thumb after the hand is complete. The gusset gives a better anatomical fit at the base of the thumb.
A method for knitting small circumferences in the round on one long circular needle. The cable is pulled into a loop at the midpoint so each half of the stitches sits on its own needle tip.
An increase worked by lifting the horizontal strand between two stitches with the left needle and knitting into the back of it. M1L lifts from left to right; M1R lifts from right to left.

content.text: Seamless wrist warmers in 1x1 rib worked in the round, with a small
gusseted thumb
opening, sized for wrist circumferences of 16, 18, and 20 cm.
The construction is worked in the round using
magic loop

on a long circular. A small gusset of 8 stitches is increased over 6 rounds then placed on waste yarn; the wrist continues upward and the gusset stitches are picked up and bound off separately. The gusset makes the opening large enough to slide the thumb through without puckering the fabric. Budget about 70 g (155 m / 170 yards) of DK wool for the pair.
What you need

items.name: Yarn
items.qty: 70 g (about 155 m / 170 yards) of DK-weight wool

items.name: Needles
items.qty: 3.75 mm (UK 9 / US 5) circular needle, at least 80 cm cable, for magic loop

items.name: Stitch markers
items.qty: 3: 1 for beginning of round, 2 to flank the thumb gusset

items.name: Waste yarn
items.qty: About 30 cm of smooth contrasting yarn

content.text: Gauge
22 stitches and 30 rounds to 10 cm in 1x1 rib slightly stretched on 3.75 mm needles.
Stitches used
Pattern
Before you cast on, circle your size. Every stitch count reads S (M, L) for wrist circumferences 16 (18, 20) cm.
Cast on and lower cuff
Using the long-tail cast-on, cast on 34 (38, 42) stitches. Join to work in the round. Work 1x1 rib for 24 (26, 28) rounds.
Thumb gusset
Place gusset markers flanking the first 2 stitches of the round. These 2 stitches are the seed of the gusset.
Increase round: SM,
M1R
, work 2 rib stitches, M1L, SM, continue in 1x1 rib to end. Work 2 plain rounds. Repeat the increase once more. Gusset holds 6 stitches.
Place the 6 gusset stitches on waste yarn. Cast on 2 stitches over the gap using backward-loop cast-on. Continue in 1x1 rib for 20 (22, 24) rounds. Bind off in rib.
Thumb edging
Return the 6 gusset stitches to the needles. Pick up 2 stitches from the bridging cast-on. Total: 8 stitches. Work 4 rounds of 1x1 rib. Bind off in rib.
Mirror your second wrist warmer

Place the gusset markers at the end of the round instead of the beginning for the second wrist warmer. Hold the first wrist warmer with the thumb gap to your right; the second should have the gap to your left.
Common faults
Thumb gap too tight: the gusset was bound off rather than placed on waste yarn for a separate thumb edging. Place the gusset stitches on waste yarn before binding off the hand.
Rib misaligned after the thumb gap: the bridging cast-on stitches land on the wrong rib column. Choose a backward-loop stitch count (2 here) that keeps the k1, p1 pattern continuous across the gap.
Finishing
Weave in all tails on the wrong side.
Care
Hand wash in cool water. Lay flat to dry.
What to try next
Extending the upper cuff to cover the fingers and binding off the finger columns individually gives you a basic fingerless glove. The gusset construction used here is the same.
